newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ING to leave Mendes Gans stake at 55 pct.
newsitem.headline: ING to leave Mendes Gans stake at 55 pct.

text.p: Dutch financial services giant Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV (ING) said on Monday it had no immediate plans to lift its stake in small Dutch cash management bank Mendes Gans above 55 percent.
ING earlier announced it was close to buying the 20 percent shareholding owned by Chase Manhattan Bank, which would bring ING's total shareholding in Mendes Gans to 55 percent.
Asked if ING planned to further add to this stake, an ING spokesman said: "Not for the moment."
No purchase price was mentioned. Mendes Gans shares were 500 guilders higher at 11,000 at 0955 GMT.
ING bought into Mendes Gans with the purchase in February 1995 of Dow Chemical Corp's 29 percent shareholding and it has since raised this stake through on-market buying.
Dutch giant Philips Electronics has almost 29 percent of the small bank, which provides financial services to multinational companies and institutional investors.
Shares in Mendes Gans are tightly held and rarely trade.
